a: its private aligned cases can inform blind human calibration, while capability and catalog readiness surfaces count zero MAGES engine-support evidence.
m: The MAGES family is mentioned as unsupported text-only benchmark calibration material, explicitly not as a decode, patchback, or runtime target.

a: replacing a required artifact with a plausible status string or self-planted sentinel makes the claim fail.
m: Claims are admitted only from externally observable behavior at the level named, never from status, comments, self-authored flags, IDs, or the existence of code.

a: evidence from one leg cannot satisfy a query for another, and a detector-only family remains visibly detector-only.
m: Identify, inventory, extract, patch, execute, render, localize, cost, privacy, and release claims each require evidence produced by that exact leg.

a: both corpora pass the named behavior and share no title-conditioned production branch; loss of either corpus proof removes the family claim.
m: A real engine-family capability is proven by the same mechanism on at least two independently sourced real titles.

a: bypassing decode, model dispatch, patchback, replay, or render with an intermediate fixture makes the composed receipt invalid.
m: An end-to-end claim exercises the exact production composition from source input through every named seam to its observable output.

a: a placeholder-rejection mutation scans artifact bytes and fails each planted stand-in despite valid-looking metadata.
m: Placeholder strings, fake binaries, synthetic provider prose, copied expected values, empty artifacts, and run-ID substrings cannot count as product evidence.

a: mutation probes that erase state change, return the expected object, skip parsing, or produce a blank frame each fail the intended test.
m: Every critical test has a documented core behavior whose removal or trivialization makes it red.

a: missing corpora, ignored suites, compiled-out tests, empty selections, and zero-assertion runs cannot report pass.
m: Gates report and enforce nonzero test, corpus, unit, scene, assertion, and artifact counts where proof requires them.

a: removing each required input makes its authoritative gate fail before a positive claim is emitted.
m: Required DBs, browsers, corpora, vault entries, credentials, fixtures, and reference artifacts fail or produce an explicit non-proof state rather than skip-as-success.

a: mutations targeting optional-looking fields, database decode errors, serialization errors, and absent statuses all yield typed failures or exact findings.
m: Missing, malformed, undecodable, or unresolved values never become zero, empty, unknown sentinels, fallback success, or dropped rows through permissive defaults.

a: injected source, DB, decode, graphics, and artifact failures are observed at the caller and prevent misleading success.
m: Production paths do not discard relevant errors with permissive option conversion, row filtering, unchecked result drops, or broad catch-and-continue behavior.

a: a fixture for every category produces its exact stable code and classifier behavior is independent of message text.
m: Invalid input, unsupported profile, in-profile defect, stale source, privacy denial, permission denial, operational pause, timeout, cancellation, budget, and internal failure remain distinct.

a: grouped fuzz and adversarial corpora across all shipped entrypoints produce zero panic, abort, unchecked allocation, overflow, recursion exhaustion, or out-of-bounds access.
m: Every decoder, schema boundary, archive reader, parser, renderer, and path function returns bounded typed errors for attacker-controlled input.

a: boundary and just-over-bound fixtures take the correct success/failure paths without truncation, clamping, saturation-induced acceptance, or resource blowup.
m: Lengths, dimensions, offsets, recursion, allocation, artifact bytes, time, output size, and process data are checked before consumption.

a: replacing the target guard with a different upstream failure makes the negative test fail.
m: Negative tests assert the intended semantic reason rather than accepting any failure from an earlier unrelated layer.

a: a dependency/symbol scan finds one canonical producer and consumer per contract and no deprecated alias or legacy outcome is emitted.
m: Retired patch, runtime, provider, schema, orchestration, result, and workflow paths cannot remain as parallel producers or compatibility shims.

a: reachability coverage touches every retained variant and fails on an unreachable or producerless case.
m: Documented enums, diagnostics, capability reasons, configuration entries, and public fields are constructible and consumed or removed.

a: generated positive and negative fixtures receive the same outcome at every implementation boundary.
m: Rust, TypeScript, JSON Schema, OpenAPI, SQL, CLI, and HTTP boundaries share exact required fields, enums, timestamps, IDs, offsets, and error semantics.

a: one mutation for every strictness class returns the specified client error before business logic or persistence.
m: Unknown fields, arbitrary enums, unvalidated timestamps, permissive objects, malformed unions, unknown query parameters, and route/method mismatches are rejected at entry.

a: every registered route ID appears in generation and live validation, and a route-specific schema fork or omission fails CI.
m: One API schema source generates complete OpenAPI and JSON Schema for every route and read model with guard parity.

a: success, malformed, permission, not-found, conflict, method, pagination, and redaction cases pass over actual HTTP and fail when routing or serialization is bypassed.
m: API behavior is exercised through a real server transport and database, not only direct services or mocked fetch.

a: a classifier detects DB, browser, provider, filesystem, and network dependencies from execution and rejects a suite whose declared class hides them.
m: Tests are classified by observable contract and dependency boundary rather than misleading unit/integration labels.

a: each critical flow completes against the real service and a broken route, permission, or backend write makes its browser test fail.
m: Core shell, onboarding, Studio, review, play, runtime, search, settings, and handoff flows have production-wiring Playwright coverage.

a: all public components have stories, changed pixels require an explicit baseline decision, and missing forwarded DOM/data attributes fail behavior tests.
m: Design-system components render in an isolated story harness with deterministic interaction and baseline images.

a: blank, tofu, placeholder, noisy decode, offscreen text, and noninteractive-choice frames are rejected by deterministic checks plus a recorded human or admitted vision verdict.
m: Render evidence is inspected for semantic coherence, legibility, correct art, translated text, glyphs, layout, choices, and redaction, not merely file existence.

a: a blank or uniformly colored frame with the right count fails the golden while the expected composed scene passes.
m: Runtime wiring tests assert dimensions and meaningful pixel hashes/content rather than capture counts alone.

a: removing one known-populated field changes the report and fails the stated completeness threshold rather than hiding behind aggregate success.
m: Real runs report populated, source-absent, extractor-missing, invalid, and unknown counts for every claimed output field.

a: the scale run exercises the named order of magnitude and a tiny fixture cannot satisfy its receipt.
m: A claimed whole-game, multi-project, or high-concurrency capability is tested at that scale with exact inputs, outputs, failures, throughput, and costs.

a: two clean-worktree replays yield identical IDs, manifests, bridge, patch, traces, scorecard, and aggregate values.
m: Given the same immutable inputs, config, model replay, and toolchain, non-provider artifacts and decisions reproduce byte-for-byte.

a: unchanged data meets byte or declared semantic equivalence, intended edits are isolated, and each corruption/mutation produces the expected failure.
m: Formats and state contracts have unchanged roundtrip, targeted edit, corruption, boundary, and implementation-killing mutations.

a: every declared comparison agrees over its corpus and a one-bit or one-rule mutation is detected.
m: Independent implementations, reference tools, oracles, encoders, and generated cases cross-check codecs, parsers, offsets, semantics, and renderers.

a: the proof graph identifies separate producers, and copying implementation output into expected data invalidates provenance.
m: Reference tools and expected results are independent of the implementation under test and are used only within lawful development validation.

a: absent evidence remains absent/unknown, conflicting sources remain linked, and a hardcoded or importer-default fact fails provenance validation.
m: Catalog, corpus, provider, benchmark, runtime, and conflict facts retain their actual source and never invent language, provider, cost, conflict kind, or identity defaults.

a: every invalid or raced request leaves no file, feedback, queue, outbox, cost, or database orphan.
m: Authorization, ownership, identity, source revision, schema, capability, path, and conflict checks occur transactionally before writes or external effects.

a: deletion, revocation, reassignment, and competing writers inserted between precheck and commit yield zero unauthorized or duplicate updates.
m: Repository mutations revalidate active subject, ownership, lease, deduplication, source identity, and conflict evidence inside the committing transaction.

a: every selected corpus resolves a complete provenance record and an unclassified corpus is inadmissible.
m: Real and derived corpora record acquisition class, lawful use, engine/profile, identities, hashes, manifests, privacy, and permitted test lanes.

a: readiness accounting lists independent corpus hashes and profile diversity, while a single-title family cannot satisfy admission.
m: Each claimed family has a corpus-acquisition inventory for at least two real validation titles and further diversity for broader claims.

a: deterministic regeneration matches every hash and a same-commit self-authored fixture cannot alone prove real readiness.
m: Public fixtures record license, source mode, generator ownership, file hashes, expected artifacts, limitations, and regeneration command.

a: public CI completes without vault access and scans find no retail text/image/audio/archive bytes; private proof links via safe hashes.
m: Redistributable synthetic fixtures run publicly, while retail bytes and full-fidelity evidence remain in gated private storage.

a: every real observed component maps to one catalog entry and every catalog entry is observed or explicitly marked specification-only rather than counted.
m: Each engine family inventories the distinct archive, codec, opcode, expression, surface, choice, asset, renderer, and failure components observed across real corpora.

a: coverage over the synthetic equals the declared component catalog and deleting one component creates a named gap.
m: Publishable synthetic corpora contain each unique in-profile component at least once with structurally faithful composition.

a: parsers, coverage maps, semantic outputs, and mutation sensitivity agree between corresponding real and synthetic components.
m: Synthetic fixtures are derived from understanding of, and differentially validated against, real behavior rather than merely resembling file headers.

a: the oracle runs every claimed real component and any synthetic/real divergence fails readiness and opens an exact gap.
m: Gated periodic lanes revalidate synthetic strength and family claims on actual private corpora.

a: a relevant code mutation fails the per-gate synthetic lane and lane runtime remains bounded without relying on absent private bytes.
m: Fast per-change gates use coverage-complete synthetic archives after differential qualification.

a: repeated parallel runs observe stable source hashes while a deliberately broken implementation still makes the mutation lane red.
m: Differential and mutation tests operate on copied inputs or isolated workspaces, never modifying a source read concurrently by another lane.

a: regeneration updates all dependents deterministically and a mixed-lineage artifact set fails before comparison.
m: Golden bridge, patch, runtime, API, benchmark, and visual artifacts share a reproducible manifest and source revision.

a: a fresh worktree resolves every retained reference and validators reject home, scratch, drive-letter, log, or stale temp paths.
m: Evidence uses content hashes, managed URIs, external IDs/URLs, or repository/run-relative paths, never checkout-local paths.

a: tampering, a malicious URI, symlink escape, wrong kind, or over-budget file fails ingestion without partial persistence.
m: Managed artifacts have verified hashes, declared kind/privacy, canonical containment, traversal resistance, size limits, and immutable promotion.

a: deleting or contradicting any required binding removes the matrix cell rather than leaving a hardcoded boolean.
m: Each advertised family/profile capability has a machine-readable receipt binding inputs, implementation, observations, limitations, fixtures/corpora, and evidence class.

a: a zero-byte delegated launcher can pass its own transport conformance but contributes zero decode/readiness titles.
m: Delegation ports and fixture engines cannot count as native decode, patch, or multi-title evidence.

a: planted raw source/target text, prompts, responses, keys, tokens, personal data, absolute paths, filenames, roots, and nested metadata are absent after every boundary.
m: Logs, errors, APIs, provider artifacts, runtime evidence, catalog output, proof bundles, and dashboards expose only allowlisted safe fields.

a: a safe diagnostic remains sufficient to reproduce the class, while a planted secret beside it is removed.
m: Redaction retains non-sensitive engine/profile, failure class, remediation, bounded counts, and support-boundary text.

a: a public bundle fails if it contains a full retail asset or recoverable passage and still carries enough hashes/metrics to verify the private run.
m: Complete game text, bytes, frames, art, audio, and derived reconstruction data remain local/private; public artifacts are non-reconstructive redacted derivatives.

a: crypt and provider operations succeed, then memory/drop and artifact/log scans find no raw, hexadecimal, base64, or transformed secret.
m: Secrets use controlled resolution, non-cloneable zeroizing holders, encoded-form leak scans, debug redaction, and no persistence.

a: traversal, symlink, hard-link alias, UNC/drive, dot segment, nested-data-root, and existing-destination fixtures fail before writes.
m: All user, archive, vault, scratch, output, artifact, env-file, and download paths use canonical no-follow containment and collision rules.

a: adding an unregistered route or repository method fails the matrix, and denial tests cover every matrix row against a real DB.
m: Every API/repository mutation and sensitive read maps to a data-driven permission and active-subject rule.

a: planted alias, commented grant, bare SQL expression, hardcoded role branch, or repository-key collision is caught.
m: Permission and no-role guards understand aliases, comments, SQL expressions, helper indirection, and AST branch shapes.

a: a write-authorized/read-denied actor can mutate the allowed field but cannot observe protected cost, routing, TM, or status data in the response.
m: Read-only requests use read-only services and response permissions independently of any mutation permission.

a: disabling a principal immediately denies protected reads/writes and revokes or invalidates its active sessions.
m: Disabled, revoked, removed, or namespace-invalid principals cannot retain effective grants or sessions.

a: a seeded multi-channel PII corpus yields no recoverable identifier in public or model-bound output while keeping non-PII issue detail.
m: Community and account data redact email, phone, handles, invite tokens, and other configured personal identifiers across domestic and international forms.

a: a golden live call satisfies every control; removing one required control quarantines the response and fails the qualifying run.
m: Operational provider admission verifies headers, request posture, served pair, storage policy, retention behavior, and response lineage for real calls.

a: the public report recomputes declared aggregates and privacy scans recover no private content.
m: Public telemetry and scorecards carry IDs, hashes, counts, durations, classes, and billed aggregates without prompt, response, Wiki, or game content.

a: response, call ledger, artifact, project/run aggregate, benchmark, and dashboard reconcile at full precision, including retries, cache, fallback, and zero-cost replay.
m: No production or proof surface fabricates, rounds into authority, double-discounts, or silently zeros billed cost.

a: guards catch scalar/object/multiline fabrication and every positive count resolves to an actual provider or admitted tokenizer record.
m: Provider token fields preserve provenance and absent values never become heuristic or zero counts.

a: cost guards catch decimal, micros, object, multiline, and bare usage shapes in every language/scope, while explicitly sourced test data carries provenance.
m: Production source and unclassified fixtures cannot embed model-price or billed-cost literals as authoritative behavior.

a: a strict scanner reaches zero active violations and a planted title-derived constant or node token fails CI.
m: Active code, schemas, CLI, environment inputs, artifacts, filenames, diagnostics, and architecture contain no game title or planning-node token as a mechanism.

a: guards fail any file over 500 lines, function over 50 lines, forbidden legacy import, node/game reference, unexplained allow, or stale compatibility path.
m: Production logic is engine-generic, typed, modular, free of speculative shims and stale task-history comments, and obeys the line budgets.

a: a benchmark run that changes a locked methodological input receives a new methodology identity and cannot be compared silently.
m: Translation evaluation has a frozen, non-self-favoring methodology covering corpora, holdout, contestants, context, metrics, judges, humans, cost, validity, and reporting.

a: every contestant resolves the same unit set and a leakage audit proves held-out units were absent from development inputs.
m: Source, fan, official, machine, and product translations align to common private units with a locked untuned holdout.

a: judges cannot recover provenance before de-anonymization and all contestants cover the same evaluated units.
m: Raw MTL, fan-edited MTL, official, product, and context-ablation contestants are anonymized and randomized under identical unit/context constraints.

a: serialized judge inputs are equal across contestants except anonymous candidate text and contain no product Wiki/analysis fields.
m: Judges receive identical deterministic source, speaker, scene, branch, and technical context but no product-generated interpretive advantage.

a: repeated scoring is byte-identical and each seeded defect changes its intended metric.
m: Terminology, entities, residue, layout, speaker, branch, technical validity, backtranslation, and other non-judge metrics are reproducible and mutation-sensitive.

a: every judgment validates against dimension-specific anchors and cannot collapse into one unexplained scalar.
m: Adequacy, fluency, register, voice, terminology, honorifics, cultural adaptation, wordplay, continuity, and build fidelity use anchored independent dimensions.

a: the minimum family diversity executes and a single-family or provenance-visible panel is invalid.
m: The live blind multi-family judge panel was retired in favor of frozen-label offline calibration, while subjective quality measurement remains separately unimplemented.

a: the report quantifies agreement, error, and divergence against frozen labels and swapping provenance labels does not change the correct outcome.
m: Frozen blind human labels calibrate model reviewers and contested official-versus-fan cases remain human-adjudicated rather than provenance-decided.

a: calibration reports false-positive/negative and preference bias by defect class, and exceeding the locked bound fails admission.
m: When the producing model also reviews, bias is measured against frozen human labels and cross-family controls.

a: seeded meaning loss triggers the tripwire with served-pair/cost evidence, while a clean paraphrase is not automatically condemned.
m: A real privacy-admitted backtranslation provides a supplemental meaning-loss signal without being treated as ground truth.

a: failure of any sensitivity, invariance, or calibration check invalidates the benchmark result.
m: The evaluation must detect deliberate sabotage, remain stable under order/provenance/judge swaps within bounds, and correlate with human anchors.

a: one run traverses every facility leg with consistent contestant/unit identities and fails on a dangling handle.
m: Seed selection, contestants, context feed, metrics, panel, calibration, aggregation, de-anonymization, cost/latency, and backlog compose without hand-authored intermediate truth.

a: every live point is provider-artifact traceable and no estimate or missing cost is plotted as zero.
m: Benchmark output reports measured quality alongside exact billed cost, latency, tokens, and cache per contestant/configuration.

a: every below-threshold dimension produces an actionable item tied to affected units rather than a generic score-only recommendation.
m: Evaluation failures become ranked, evidence-linked defect classes, likely causes, candidate fixes, and regression observations.

a: a qualifying run meets every locked threshold and removing one required evidence item makes the scorecard fail.
m: A frozen scorecard combines configured-scope coverage, deterministic correctness, Wiki/bible completeness, reviewer calibration, privacy, ZDR, cost, runtime evidence, and human anchors.

a: the gate names every failed dimension and cannot pass by compensating a zero required dimension with high unrelated scores.
m: Product readiness is expressed as evidence-backed confidence with exact gaps, not status, self-assessment, or a permissive average.
